notes:
• Evade checks replace swerve checks. A rider no longer rolls to save themselves from any crash: a wall, a barrier or a trail that was there when the round began wrecks the bike, and a bike that has boxed itself in gets no roll. The Piloting check is for being cut off: another bike lays a trail across the rider's path during the round, or comes for the same space.
  • An evade is three screens. "Collision Imminent!" holds the round, with the bikes ridden up to that moment, until the rider clicks Roll to Evade. The result is then written on the button, in red if the check failed. A check that is made brings up the Evade screen; one that is not wrecks the bike.
  • In Starfinder 2e a character who fails the check and has a Hero Point sees the button flash, and can click it again to spend the point and roll once more.
  • A rider who makes the check chooses what to do: stop, or turn left or right and finish the move that way. The map shows where each turn would go. The choice is a direction pad on screen, answered by a click or the arrow keys.
  • With a lock-in timer on, each step has 20 seconds. The GM can answer for any rider; autopilots roll and choose for themselves.
  • An evade check's DC is 15 plus 1 for every space the rider still had to cover when they were cut off, so being caught early in a long move is harder to get out of. It no longer goes by the rider's level, and no longer gets harder with every check in a match.
  • The Piloting check at the start of each round is against DC 15 in Starfinder 2e for every rider. It used to be the standard DC for the rider's level, which put a spare space out of reach of a high-level character with no training.

Full details in the release notes.
